idea-plugin.name: Environment-Specific Constant Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on a hardcoded URL or host:port string literal in Java source that also appears, textually, as a value in one of the project's own config files (.properties/.yml/.yaml/ .env) -- the value clearly belongs to config, and the code copy can now silently drift out of sync with it.

Real, documented impact: configuration/IaC drift -- a value that one day gets updated only in the config file (the "correct" place) leaves real code still pointing at the old endpoint/port, with no compile error to catch it. Adjacent to this catalog's own config-secrets-file-companion/ env-diff-companion, but neither checks specifically for code-vs-config value divergence.

Stated honestly: v0.1 matches only full URLs (http(s)://...) and explicit host:port pairs -- never a bare port number without host context, to keep the false-positive rate low. Exact string match only against config values found in .properties/.yml/.yaml files and the single exact filename .env (no .env.* variants yet).

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

localInspection.displayName: Hardcoded literal duplicates a config value
